newsitem.title: RUSSIA: IMF mission due to arrive Moscow July 22 -Tass.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission due to arrive Moscow July 22 -Tass.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund mission will arrive in Moscow on July 22 to assess prospects for disbursing a new tranche from its $10 billion loan to Russia, Itar-Tass news agency said on Tuesday.

It quoted IMF Moscow representative Martin Gilman as saying IMF experts thought the Russian economy could start growing in 1997 and delays with the disbursement of the $700 million tranche would be unlikely.
The IMF has in the past suspended paying several tranches of its Extended Financing Facility programme to Russia following low tax revenues. The tranches were later paid.
Russian officials have forecast 1997 would be the first year of growth, with gross domestic product, or GDP, capable of rising four percent.
The State Statistics Committee said on Tuesday that June GDP rose four percent compared to May. But GDP fell by 0.2 percent in the first half of 1997 year-on-year, it said.
Tass quoted Gilman as saying the mission would focus on tax revenues and the success of structural reforms during its 10-day visit.
Gilman said the IMF had paid Russia about $3.7 billion in 1996 and $1.35 billion in 1997.
